title: Correctness of the dual-rail construction
statement: Let $n$ be the number of input variables and choose an input coordinate. Suppose a list of gates is acyclic, meaning that the arguments of its gate at position $i$ all have index less than $n+i$, and that each gate has at most two arguments. Then the construction that processes these gates produces statements and rails satisfying the dual-rail invariant: one rail pair per input or gate vertex, valid references, rails computing each vertex's value and its complement for every input assignment, and at most twice as many statements as gates.
